 Canaveral Port Authority Donates Firefighting Equipment to EFSC Fire Training Center
October 19, 2026 
 The Canaveral Port Authority today officially turned over the ceremonial keys to “Truck
 52,” an aerial fire apparatus formerly operated by Canaveral Fire Rescue, to Eastern
 Florida State College (EFSC) for use in the school’s Fire Training Center. The donation
 was formally recognized during a ceremony today at Port Canaveral, where Port Canaveral
 CEO Capt. John Murray and Canaveral Fire Rescue Deputy Fire Chief Jeff Crawley presented
 a ceremonial key to Eastern Florida State College Vice President External Affairs
 Jack Parker. 
 “We are proud to donate this valuable equipment to support Eastern Florida’s education
 and training program,” said Capt. John Murray, Port Canaveral CEO. “Truck 52 served
 our Port community well, and it will continue to be of service in preparing the next
 generation of firefighters and first responders for their vitally important careers.”
 The apparatus, formerly known as “Canaveral Fire Rescue Truck 52,” is a 2012 model
 year 75-foot Pierce Velocity ladder truck, which was purchased by the Canaveral Port
 Authority and operated by Canaveral Fire Rescue. During its time in service, the truck
 and its complement of Canaveral Fire Rescue firefighters has responded to nearly 7,000
 calls throughout Brevard County because of Port Canaveral’s mutual aid and automatic
 aid agreements with 26 communities and federal government installations including
 Kennedy Space Center, NASA, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Patrick Space Force
 Base, and U.S. Navy’s Naval Ordnance Test Unit (NOTU).
 "Although this truck's assignment is changing, its mission remains the same: serving
 others. We are proud to be part of the handover of this apparatus so it can continue
 making a difference and helping firefighters answer the call when their community
 needs them most,” said Chris Quinn, Fire Chief, Canaveral Fire Rescue. 
 The donated firetruck will be incorporated into EFSC’s firefighter and emergency response
 training programs, providing students and trainees with valuable hands-on training
 experience required to become a state certified firefighter in Florida. In addition
 to offering a Fire Science associate’s degree, the college operates a fire training
 center and Fire Fighter I/II Certificate Program and Continuing Education Fire Science
 courses to advance firefighter professional skills.
 “Eastern Florida State College is grateful to the Canaveral Port Authority and Canaveral
 Fire Rescue for the donation of Truck 52 which will help our students gain valuable
 hands-on experience for their future careers,” said Dr. James Richey, President of
 EFSC.  “Support from partners like the Canaveral Port Authority and Canaveral Fire
 Rescue are critical to our ongoing efforts to train and educate the next generation
 of firefighters and first responders.” 
 The Pierce Velocity ladder truck is equipped with a 2,000 GPM (gallon-per-minute)
 pumping capacity with a 400-gallon tank and can carry up to 1,000 feet of five-inch
 supply hose. Built in Appleton, Wisc., the truck’s 75-foot aerial ladder provides
 nearly 68 feet of horizontal reach, giving instructors and students the ability to
 conduct a wide range of practical training evolutions involving elevated rescue, fire
 suppression and aerial operations.
 Port Canaveral has donated firefighting assets in previous years, including a Pierce
 Lance fire truck and a fire pumper to the Monticello Volunteer Fire Department in
 Jefferson County, Fla.
 The donation to EFSC’s training program reflects Port Canaveral and Canaveral Fire
 Rescue’s continuous commitment to supporting firefighter education, emergency preparedness
 and first responder training throughout the region. The Port also underwrites specialized
 on-site liquefied natural gas firefighting training for cruise lines and other organizations.
